explanations.answer: He stations troops in every fortified city
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Jehoshaphat stationed troops in every fortified city of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:2). Every fortified city, not just a few of them. That's a king who means business.

explanations.answer: He sends silver to the king of Aram
explanations.explanation: Silver for Aram's king isn't in this passage, friend. Here the new king's strength is troops and garrisons inside his own land. I get the guess, since kings and silver go together like dough and a hungry kid. But the text says he stationed troops in every fortified city of Judah.

Not this time. The text doesn't mention Egypt or hired soldiers anywhere in these verses. Jehoshaphat stationed troops in every fortified city of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:2). The strength comes from his own cities and his own land.

True! Jehoshaphat put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured (2 Chronicles 17:2). Asa captured them and Jehoshaphat guards them. Now THAT'S a family business.

This one's true, friend. The text says he put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured (2 Chronicles 17:2). So Asa's captured cities get guarded too. Easy one to second-guess, and I'd have blinked too.

explanations.answer: He walked in the earlier ways of King David
explanations.explanation: That's it. The text says the LORD was with Jehoshaphat “…because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David.” (2 Chronicles 17:3). Notice the word earlier. The text says David's earlier ways. Plain and simple, and no troop count needed.

explanations.answer: He brought gold back to the temple
explanations.explanation: Gold for the temple doesn't show up in these verses, friend. The text gives the reason straight: “…because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David.” (2 Chronicles 17:3). Gold sounds impressive, but the reason is how he walked.

explanations.answer: He rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: Walls are a fine guess for a king, but they aren't the reason here. Nothing in this passage says he rebuilt Jerusalem's walls. The text says the LORD was with him “…because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David.” (2 Chronicles 17:3).
Not quite, friend. The text says Jehoshaphat did not seek the Baals (2 Chronicles 17:3). No side hustle with false gods, either. Verse 4 says he sought the God of his father instead.

Right. Jehoshaphat did not seek the Baals, the false gods (2 Chronicles 17:3). He sought the God of his father instead (2 Chronicles 17:4). No secret side-deal, and no sneaking off when nobody's looking.

Yes! The text says he “…walked by His commandments rather than the practices of Israel.” (2 Chronicles 17:4). Israel is the same Israel he was strengthening himself against back in verse 1, and he doesn't copy their practices either. He follows God's commandments, not the neighbors.

Egypt is a fair guess, since it's a famous neighbor. But the text names a different kingdom here. He “…walked by His commandments rather than the practices of Israel.” (2 Chronicles 17:4). Israel is the answer, friend.

Moab doesn't come up in this verse. The text says he “…walked by His commandments rather than the practices of Israel.” (2 Chronicles 17:4). Israel is the one named, the same Israel Jehoshaphat was already strengthening himself against (2 Chronicles 17:1).

True! The LORD established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought him tribute (2 Chronicles 17:5). That means the whole of Judah, not just the folks nearby. Imagine your whole neighborhood showing up at your door with gifts.

It's actually true, friend. The text says the LORD established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought him tribute (2 Chronicles 17:5). All of Judah, not just a few. The riches and honor follow right after.

explanations.answer: The high places and Asherah poles
explanations.explanation: You got it. The text says he removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah (2 Chronicles 17:6). Right before that, the verse says his heart took delight in the ways of the LORD. Those two things sit side by side in the same verse.

explanations.answer: The golden calves of Bethel and Dan
explanations.explanation: Those aren't in this passage, friend. The text says he removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah (2 Chronicles 17:6). The removal here is inside Judah's own land. Stick with what the verse names.

explanations.answer: The idols of Moab and Ammon
explanations.explanation: Moab and Ammon aren't mentioned in this verse. The text says he removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah (2 Chronicles 17:6). That's the cleanup it names, right at home in Judah.

Teach is right. Jehoshaphat sent them to teach in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7). With a king who has all those troops, you'd expect a march, but this team went out to teach. Five officials, nine Levites and two priests, and not one of them was sent to fight. That's a whole lot of teachers.

I see why you'd go there, with all those troops around. But the text says Jehoshaphat sent these officials, Levites and priests out to teach in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7). Teaching is the job it gives this team. They went out to teach.

Building does show up later in the passage, when he builds fortresses and store cities (2 Chronicles 17:12). But this team had a different job. Jehoshaphat sent them out to teach in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7).

explanations.answer: The Book of the Law of the LORD
explanations.explanation: That's the one. The text says they went through the towns of Judah “…taking with them the Book of the Law of the LORD.” (2 Chronicles 17:9). The Book went with them. And they taught the people in every one of those towns.

The ark is a holy thing, but this passage doesn't say the team carried it. The text says they were “…taking with them the Book of the Law of the LORD.” (2 Chronicles 17:9). The Book of the Law is the answer, friend.
The bronze serpent isn't in this passage, friend. The text says they were “…taking with them the Book of the Law of the LORD.” (2 Chronicles 17:9). Their teaching went with the Book in hand.

Not this time, friend. The text says the dread of the LORD fell on the surrounding kingdoms, “…so that they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.” (2 Chronicles 17:10). No war came. The dread of the LORD is what the verse names.

Correct. The dread of the LORD fell on the kingdoms around Judah, “…so that they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.” (2 Chronicles 17:10). Not one of them marched in. All those troops, and the verse puts the quiet down to the dread of the LORD.

explanations.answer: Rams and goats from their flocks
explanations.explanation: Yes! The Arabs brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats from their flocks (2 Chronicles 17:11). That's 7,700 of each. If somebody handed me that many of anything, I'd need a bigger kitchen.

Camels and spices sound like a believable gift, but they aren't in this verse. The Arabs brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats from their flocks (2 Chronicles 17:11). No spice rack, friend. This gift came with hooves.

Horses and chariots aren't in this verse, and Egypt isn't either. Some Philistines brought gifts and silver, and the Arabs brought 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats from their flocks (2 Chronicles 17:11). The Arabs' gift was livestock, friend.

That's it. The text says Jehoshaphat grew stronger and stronger, and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah (2 Chronicles 17:12). Stronger and stronger, and the building shows it. Then verse 13 says he kept vast supplies in the cities of Judah.
Palaces would be a nice touch for a rich king, but the text doesn't say he built any. It says he built fortresses and store cities in Judah (2 Chronicles 17:12). Fortresses is the answer.

Markets would make sense with all that tribute coming in, but the verse doesn't say it. Jehoshaphat built fortresses and store cities in Judah (2 Chronicles 17:12). The next verse says he kept vast supplies in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:13).
